# Agent N's Hermes News — 2026-10-17

**Executive summary:** A hardware-launch-level day. **@NousResearch** announced **Hermes Agent** as a [launch partner for **NVIDIA RTX Spark**](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-eb6add8182a2) across the new generation of laptops — the week's runaway top social post (1,013 likes) — reinforced by official amplification of **@zacbowden**'s in-depth [**Windows Central** review](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-b994a88307a6), extended [video coverage of hardware and security](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-49831796d9c8), and a reply teasing [**OpenShell** and **MXC**](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-6aeac627fd03) as upcoming products. Grounding note: the story rests entirely on official social channels this cycle, with no independent news or research corroboration — quote specifics as announced. The product story is a feedback loop working in public: after community pushback, **@Teknium** reversed the new [**90-day session auto-prune**](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-33ea1f4fe9b0) (now off by default, replaced by storage-aware prompting) and candidly explained how [unbounded local session databases had been filling users' disks and blocking sessions](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-a9bb334c6a24) — a [fix is confirmed for the next release](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-b4ac47aa9bc1), with **cron** scheduling work and the daily-cleaned `.hermes/cache/scratch` directory rounding out the storage story, and sentiment strongly rewarded the fast turnaround. The ecosystem boom is the widest cross-category theme: [**verso** (open-source orchestrator)](/?date=2026-10-17&category=research#item-hn-49628094), **@rlaope**'s [**deepseek-bot** launch on **deepseek-harness**](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-5d4f3f74b75c) and an [**Oh-My-Hermes** deep-dive guide](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-b51fb165d53c), **@tonbistudio**'s ~20K-view [**Reverse Engineer Anything** guide](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-ba61b5a396ce), plus the carried [**LanceDB**](/?date=2026-10-15&category=research#item-hn-49133145) and [**grafana-agento11y-hermes**](/?date=2026-10-15&category=research#item-hn-49318128) stack. Ultrafast hype centered on [**DeepSeek V4.1 Flash** at 848+ TPS](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-034c1dd8dbe5) — speed coverage of an existing release (GA 2026-09-10) — while [**GLM-5.3-flash-ultrafast** (525 TPS)](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-97d9c9fefec1) could not be verified against the model roster (tops out at **GLM-5.2**) and stays unconfirmed. The news feed ran quiet ([automated daily sync](/?date=2026-10-17&category=news#item-12e52f1275e3) only; no releases, no merged PRs), and the research feed re-anchored on **v0.20.0**'s docs bundle — carried reference, not a fresh launch. Net read: a positioning headline plus a visible listen-and-reverse product loop. Practical agenda: confirm session auto-prune is off and audit disk usage, keep **v0.22.2** as your build, verify **GLM-5.3** speed claims before relying on them, and mind the carried adversarial/looping reports if you run agents unattended.

## Releases

No new tags today — the news feed was a quiet maintenance cycle with only the [automated daily-sync commit](/?date=2026-10-17&category=news#item-12e52f1275e3). The standing picture holds: **v0.22.2** remains the build to run (the [corrective release](/?date=2026-10-16&category=news#item-b93627ac4347) after **v0.22.1** was built from the wrong commit), so don't go chasing older tags.

Two forward-looking notes from the product loop: the [session-management fix **@Teknium** confirmed](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-b4ac47aa9bc1) (auto-prune off by default, storage-aware prompting) is slated for the **next release**, alongside [**cron** scheduling work](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-e19a0c47dbe7).

One framing note worth making explicit: the research feed re-centers on **Hermes Agent v0.20.0** as a "flagship release," but this is the [official docs bundle](/?date=2026-10-16&category=research#item-hn-49159200) (GitHub tag **v2026.8.3**) catching up — [**Claude Pro/Max** subscription auth](/?date=2026-10-16&category=research#item-hn-49790991) and [**Hermes Kanban** multi-agent profile collaboration](/?date=2026-10-16&category=research#item-hn-49604068) are documented carried support, not a fresh launch, and neither [**Almanac (YC S26)**](/?date=2026-10-17&category=research#item-hn-49511007) adoption nor the current stable changes that. **v0.22.2** is current; **v0.20.0** is reference material.

- **RTX Spark launch partnership:** **@NousResearch** named [**Hermes Agent** a launch partner for **NVIDIA RTX Spark**](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-eb6add8182a2) across the new generation of laptops (1,013 likes — the week's runaway top post), amplified with [**@zacbowden**'s in-depth **Windows Central** review](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-b994a88307a6) and [extended video coverage of hardware and security](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-49831796d9c8), plus replies [teasing **OpenShell** and **MXC** as upcoming products](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-6aeac627fd03). This positions Hermes as a first-class on-device agent at the hardware-launch level — but the story rests entirely on official channels this cycle with no independent corroboration yet, so treat specifics as announced.
- **Session auto-prune reversal:** after community pushback, **@Teknium** [reversed the new **90-day session auto-prune**](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-33ea1f4fe9b0) — now off by default in favor of storage-aware prompting — then candidly explained the root cause: [unbounded local session databases had been filling users' disks and blocking sessions](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-a9bb334c6a24). A [fix lands in the next release](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-b4ac47aa9bc1), [**cron** scheduling work is underway](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-e19a0c47dbe7), and [`.hermes/cache/scratch` is daily-cleaned](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-344879e6d137). Sentiment was strongly positive.
- **Ecosystem tooling boom:** new this cycle are [**verso**, an open-source orchestrator layer for knowledge work](/?date=2026-10-17&category=research#item-hn-49628094), and **@rlaope**'s [**deepseek-bot**, an open-source persistent-memory agent on the **deepseek-harness**](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-5d4f3f74b75c). They join the carried stack — [**LanceDB**-based semantic memory](/?date=2026-10-15&category=research#item-hn-49133145), [**grafana-agento11y-hermes**](/?date=2026-10-15&category=research#item-hn-49318128) observability, and the [**Refine Cycle**](/?date=2026-10-14&category=research#item-hn-49606988) self-improvement plugin — with **Teknium**'s [open plugin-maintenance offers](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-c0ad3e42da50) reinforcing a healthy builder base.
- **Guide wave:** **@rlaope** published a [deep-dive **Oh-My-Hermes (OMH)** guide](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-b51fb165d53c) (subagent routing to task-specific models, filesystem-labeled long-term memory), and [**@tonbistudio**'s **Reverse Engineer Anything** plugin guide](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-ba61b5a396ce) drew ~20K views with official amplification. **OMH** [continues its run](/?date=2026-10-16&category=social#item-b84d15a8a0b3) — **4.0.0** in preparation, **3.4k stars** as previously covered.

- **Strategy & benchmarks:** **@Teknium** [defended the six-month power-user-first build](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-2dd209adf49b) against consumer criticism and [claimed Hermes beats **Claude Code** using Claude on every reported benchmark](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-9324877d0141), often with ~3x fewer tokens — quote as his claim.
- **Community flavor:** the cryptic one-word ["**Motion.**" teaser](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-c0549400cfa5) pulled ~27.7K views; **@NousResearch** [bantered with **Andrew Yang** about open source](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-6988a3c15f77) (541 likes); an [editor's note clarified a satirical TIME-list tweet](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-92f8c87c3dd0) and restated the no-paid-placement policy; and the [**Hermes Index** was updated](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-897de9812a56) — though its "**GPT 6.1 Sol**" entry doesn't match the model roster (**GPT-6-Sol**, GA 2026-09-22), likely a naming slip.
- **Watch items (carried):** the [**hermes-jekyl-hyde** adversarial repository](/?date=2026-10-14&category=research#item-hn-49231797) demonstrating an LLM-reversal technique explicitly targeting hermes-agent, and the [Ask HN thread about a freshly provisioned agent looping on a headless Debian server](/?date=2026-10-14&category=research#item-hn-49916751) with a Z.ai **GLM** backend — hardening and onboarding-friction warnings for unattended deployments. The [~**23,000 open-PR backlog**](/?date=2026-10-16&category=research#item-hn-49424643) remains the project-health number.

## Tips & Tutorials

- **Session storage hygiene, now that auto-prune is off:** with the **90-day** auto-prune disabled by default, session databases can grow unbounded until the next release's fix lands — [`.hermes/cache/scratch` is daily-cleaned](/?date=2026-10-17&category=social#item-344879e6d137), but the session DB is on you. If you run always-on agents, check disk usage today.
- **Running **Nemotron 3.5 Super VL** locally:** following [yesterday's day-one integration](/?date=2026-10-16&category=social#item-e1857a6ca493), local-run guides landed — [LM Studio coverage](/?date=2026-10-17&category=research#item-9fff5474f526) notes a ~**70GB Q4 GGUF** and heavy RAM requirements. The model is **120B-A12B** with **BF16**/**NVFP4** checkpoints under the commercial-friendly [**OpenMDW-1.1** license](/?date=2026-10-17&category=research#item-bb6d6d51b588) (GA/API 2026-10-15). top_items.title: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Hugging Face: Checkpoints, Licence and How to Run
top_items.content:
The Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Hugging Face release gives you everything: open weights in BF16 and NVFP4, an OpenMDW-1.1 licence that allows commercial use, and recipes for vLLM, SGLang and Transformers. Nvidia also released training data and recipes. My video below covers the model. Here’s what’s on Hugging Face and how to run it.

Key takeaways

- Checkpoints: BF16 (full precision) and NVFP4 (optimised).

- Licence: OpenMDW-1.1 — commercial use allowed.

- Hardware for BF16: 4× H100 or 2× GB200.

- Community GGUF builds (e.g. Unsloth) for llama.cpp-based tools.

## What’s on Hugging Face

Repository
What it is

nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-BF16
Full-precision weights

nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4
Optimised 4-bit weights for Nvidia hardware

unsloth/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-GGUF
Community GGUF builds

Nvidia datasets
Open datasets for agentic tool use, long context, vision-language and more

## Hardware requirements

The model card lists 4× H100 or 2× GB200 GPUs on Linux (Hopper or Blackwell) for the BF16 release. The NVFP4 version is designed for more efficient deployment, including on Nvidia’s DGX Spark desktop machine. For consumer setups, use the GGUF builds in LM Studio or Ollama (70GB+).

## How to run it with vLLM

The model card’s vLLM recipe serves it with tensor parallelism across four GPUs, multi-token-prediction speculative decoding, and the served name `nemotron-3.5-super-vl` on port 8000, using the vLLM OpenAI image (nightly or v0.32.0). Tool calling uses the `qwen3_coder` parser. SGLang (v0.5.20) is supported on two GB200s, and Transformers works through the image-text-to-text pipeline with `trust_remote_code`.

## Reasoning and video settings

- Reasoning modes: off, medium or on, set with `enable_thinking` and medium effort.

- Reasoning and the answer share the token budget.

- Video: up to 256 frames at 2 FPS (1 FPS and up to 128 frames suggested for 1080p).

- Inputs: text, JPEG/PNG images, document pages and MP4 video up to 2 minutes.

## The licence

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is released under OpenMDW-1.1, and the model card says it’s ready for commercial or non-commercial use. As always, read the licence yourself before building a product on it.

## Should you self-host it?

Self-hosting makes sense for companies that need privacy, control or fine-tuning — Nvidia released the recipes to make that possible. For everyone else, OpenRouter’s free and cheap paid versions are far simpler.

Let me be clear: this is not a frontier model. It’s not going to replace Claude Opus 5.5 for your hardest work. What it is: a free, open, fast model that can read screenshots, PDFs and charts and then act on them — which is exactly the job a lot of agent work starts with.

## Fine-tuning Nemotron 3.5 Super VL

Because Nvidia released training recipes and datasets, you can fine-tune the model on your own data — your documents, your formats, your way of working. That’s most useful for companies with a specific, repeated visual task, like reading a particular kind of invoice or form. Fine-tuning a 120B model needs serious GPUs, so most teams will use cloud GPU providers rather than their own hardware.

## BF16 vs NVFP4

BF16 is the full-precision release: the best quality, but it needs the most memory. NVFP4 is a 4-bit format designed for Nvidia’s newer GPUs, cutting memory needs dramatically with little quality loss, which is what makes running it on smaller systems like DGX Spark possible. If you’re deploying on Nvidia Blackwell hardware, NVFP4 is usually the practical choice.

## Hosted alternatives

If self-hosting isn’t worth it for you, the same model is available through OpenRouter, Nvidia NIM, ModelScope and other hosts, and Together AI added it at launch. That gives you the open model without managing GPUs.

## Final thoughts

A last practical note: model cards are updated as recipes and benchmarks improve, so check the Hugging Face page for the latest serving instructions before you deploy. Nvidia’s recipes are tuned for its own hardware, and the community often publishes faster or smaller variants within days of a release — worth watching if you want to run it on less hardware.

If you just want to use the model rather than host it, skip all of this and use OpenRouter’s free or paid version, or try it free in OpenCode.

Open weights, open data and clear recipes make this one of the easiest big models to build on.

## How I’d test it this week

If you’re evaluating self-hosting, start by testing the hosted version on your real tasks. Only if it’s good enough — and you have a privacy, cost or customisation reason — is it worth renting GPUs to host it yourself.

When you do, start with the NVFP4 checkpoint on Blackwell hardware, follow the model card’s vLLM recipe, and benchmark throughput on your own prompts before committing.

## Common questions

Can I download it for free? Yes — the weights are free on Hugging Face. Can I use it commercially? The OpenMDW-1.1 licence allows commercial use, but read it yourself first. Do I need Nvidia GPUs? The official recipes target Nvidia Hopper and Blackwell GPUs; community GGUF builds run in llama.cpp-based tools like LM Studio and Ollama on other hardware. Is there a smaller version? Not of Super VL itself, but Nvidia’s Bolt 74B-A9B fits in 24GB of memory.

## The bottom line on Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Hugging Face

The Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Hugging Face release is unusually open: weights, data and recipes. If you have the GPUs, it’s a strong model to host yourself; if not, use the hosted versions.

## FAQ: nemotron 3.5 super vl hugging face

### Is Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on Hugging Face?

Yes — BF16 and NVFP4 checkpoints from Nvidia, plus community GGUF builds.

### What licence does it use?

OpenMDW-1.1, which allows commercial use.

### What hardware does it need?

4× H100 or 2× GB200 for BF16; NVFP4 is more efficient.

### Can I run it with vLLM?

Yes — the model card includes a vLLM recipe with tool calling.

### Did Nvidia release training data?

Yes — open datasets and training recipes are on Hugging Face.

### Is there a GGUF version?

Yes — community GGUF builds such as Unsloth’s are on Hugging Face, and they power the LM Studio and llama.cpp-style setups.

Both work. LM Studio gives you a friendly app with a model catalogue and chat window; Ollama gives you a simple command (`ollama run nemotron-3.5-super`) and an 80–90GB build. Pick whichever you already use — see my Ollama guide.

Start with a modest context length and increase it only as needed — bigger contexts slow things down and use more memory. Offload as much of the model to your GPU as your hardware allows. How to Get the Most Out of Oh-My-Hermes

Simply put, Oh-My-Hermes (OMH) is an intelligence pack that makes Hermes Agent insanely good just by plugging it in.

Today, instead of just a basic intro, here’s a quick guide on how to actually use it and the impact it brings.

1. Set up subagent routing 
Whether you use omh-model, omh-model-setup, or just ask the agent, OMH routes each task category to the right model (e.g., ultrabrain, visual-engineering, deep-work).
Recommended setups are in the README. Just configure the categories for your setup, and the right model will run automatically when handling subagent tasks.

2. Memory system 
OMH comes with long-term memory—turn it on, and retention goes way up.
It mixes in smart mechanics like filesystem labeling, semantic search, TTL, and more.
If you want to audit or organize what the agent remembers, try using the `memory-sync` skill. It presents stored, ambiguous, or cluttered memories so you can clean them up easily.

3. Calling tons of skills isn't recommended, but definitely know `ulw-XYZ` 
The Ultra-Work skills prefixed with `ulw-` handle loops, goal engineering via plan skills, coding rules, and parallel tasks to push execution through the most optimized path.
Other skills can be called manually or auto-routed (ulw has auto-routing too), but just dropping a quick "ulw-work let's go" into your prompt works even better.

4. The TUI looks slick
The TUI is becoming standalone. OMH’s TUI provides live viewers for parallel subagent routing, omh todo, and more. It looks great, so definitely give it a try.
